subject: Zephyr Health: resource triage — staggered autoscale vs single carveout
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T11:12:00Z
Subject: Zephyr Health: resource triage — staggered autoscale vs single carveout

Team —

Quick background: Zephyr Health (launching a clinical search feature) asked for a dedicated pool for their pilot. Their ask: 10x baseline concurrency for two weeks around launch (target date Sep 7). They want guaranteed capacity (not best-effort burst) and an SLA alignment. Attached is a proposed pool-allocation matrix they shared with numbers (zephyr_pool_matrix_v1.xlsx).

Options I see:
- Single dedicated carveout (10 GPUs) for the window — simple but heavy on committed capacity.
- Staggered mini-slices + autoscale exception: start with a 4-GPU slice + temporary autoscale ceiling of +6 GPUs for 2h-per-day peak. This reduces total reserved headroom but requires an autoscale policy exception and tighter ops guardrails.

Asking for a quick cross-functional read:
- Kimberly: can we approve an autoscale ceiling exception for a customer on a short window, and what controls/telemetry do you need?
- Marcus/Product: is staggered rollout acceptable to Zephyr or do they insist on fixed carveout?
- Marissa/CS: what is the minimum commitment Zephyr will accept to preserve their go-live confidence?

I flagged this because it touches reservations policy, SLA, and a potential precedence for other pilots. Hoping to land a decision and a runbook this week.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: zephyr_pool_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Zephyr Health: resource triage — staggered autoscale vs single carveout

Karthik —

Thanks for the summary and the matrix. A few technical clarifications before policy:
- What do their traffic curves look like? Is the 10x concurrency across many short bursts or a sustained spike?
- Are they doing long-context generation (>= 2k tokens) or short queries? (affects slot utilization)

Operationally, an autoscale "ceiling" exception is doable if we scope it tightly:
- Timeboxed window (e.g., Sep 5–Sep 12)
- Per-request token caps and request-level admission control to avoid noisy neighbors
- Preflight load test with the ops team to assert tail latency impact

If they can provide a 48-hour load test schedule we can validate. Otherwise I'd lean to a small carved base + short burst allowance rather than a full 10-GPU carveout.

Laura
Head of Dedicated Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Zephyr Health: resource triage — staggered autoscale vs single carveout

Appreciate the quick review. Some product context from my side: Zephyr is sensitive to error-rate increases and will treat any tail-latency regressions as show-stoppers. Their plan is relatively bursty: daytime query peaks aligned to clinician hours (~09:00–15:00 ET), short sessions with moderate token footprints (~200–400 tokens).

Given that, here's a proposal that balances cost and risk:
1) Baseline carveout: 4 GPUs reserved for the pilot window (Sep 5–Sep 12).
2) Controlled burst lane: allow autoscale up to 10 GPUs but gated by an internal "burst token" that Zephyr consumes from a daily allotment (e.g., enough for two 2-hour peaks). This gives them the capacity they need while letting us cap exposure.
3) Preflight: a one-day production-like load test hitting the proposed burst pattern — ops runbook attached (ops-runbook-diff.md) with the small changes we need from standard runbooks (added RBAC, circuit-break thresholds, and rollback criteria).

If ops and infra sign off on telemetry (per-request trace ids, tail-latency alerting), I think this hybrid approach works and is less precedent-setting than a full carveout. It requires: runbook sign-off, a signed SOW addendum documenting the temporary autoscale ceiling, and an ops on-call pledge during the window.

Marcus
Principal Product Manager, Serving
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-27T13:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Zephyr Health: resource triage — staggered autoscale vs single carveout

Team — quick commercial note. Zephyr is under customer pressure from their platform ops and will push if we come back with any "we can only do X". Their buyer (Amar) stated they will accept a timeboxed, well-instrumented exception if we can guarantee a postmortem and credits if we breach latency SLOs. They want the launch on Sep 8 to match a partner announcement.

From negotiation POV: I recommend we accept Marcus's hybrid approach but formalize:
- A 1-week addendum that defines burst allotment and SLA credit trigger points
- A short ramp payment (covering partial commitment) so we don't shoulder full cost if they don't use burst hours

I can draft the addendum if legal approves the template — need sign-off from capacity/infra on the operational constraints and from product on the runbook scope.

Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-08-30T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Zephyr Health: resource triage — staggered autoscale vs single carveout

All — thanks for the inputs and the attachments. After reviewing with ops and legal, I'm comfortable approving a conditional exception to the autoscale policy with these controls in place: 

Decision (approved): Hybrid approach — 4-GPU baseline carveout + autoscale ceiling to 10 GPUs for the window Sep 5–Sep 12, gated by burst-token allotment and daily caps.

Conditions (must be completed before we flip any switches):
- Signed one-week addendum (Marissa will lead) that specifies burst allotment, SLA credit tiers, and billing ramp.
- Preflight production-like load test (ops) with a greenlight checklist completed (Laura to own).
- Runbook sign-off with explicit rollback criteria and alert thresholds (Marcus to own; see ops-runbook-diff.md).
- RBAC: only Zephyr's platform service account may consume burst tokens; manual on-call escalation path documented.
- Telemetry: tail-latency p95/p99 dashboards and token consumption meter visible in console (Engineering to validate).

I'll temporarily tag this as an approved exception in the reservations tracker (will create the ticket and link to the addendum). If any of the conditions fail, the exception is revoked and we revert to the 4-GPU baseline only.

Next steps (owners):
- Marissa: draft addendum + legal loop (ETA 48h)
- Laura: schedule preflight load test and checklist (ETA 72h)
- Marcus: finalize runbook diffs and postmortem template (ETA 48h)
- Karthik: sync with Amar and confirm load-test schedule + get explicit buy-in on addendum terms (ETA 24h)

If we hit the timeline everyone will be covered for the Sep 8 partner announcement. Thanks all — please reply only with updates to your action items so we keep the thread clean.

Kimberly Park
Director, Capacity Management
Redwood Inference
